mechanism_narrative: The trough week t-1w put RETAIL_REC at -19.0, PARKS at -41.6 and RESIDENTIAL at +8.1; the t-0w reversal to -13.4, -20.0 and +5.9 breaks the downward run, and RETAIL_REC mean-reverts upward from its depressed trailing 28-day mean of about -15.5.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose 5.6 points from t-1w (-19.0) to t-0w (-13.4)
regime_hint: restriction easing with the local mobility trough breaking
failure_condition: The forward 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is at or below -15.5 even though the t-0w rebound is followed by at least one further week of non-worsening RETAIL_REC.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT was pinned near its trough (-42.9 to -46.3) for three weeks but rose 4.0 points to -42.3 at t-0w; crossing back above -45 signals commuter trips restarting, and transit-anchored retail strips recover their footfall within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean crosses above -45 (observed -46.3 at t-1w to -42.3 at t-0w)
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 4.0 points week-on-week from -46.3 to -42.3 while RETAIL_REC improved 5.6 points
regime_hint: restriction easing with commuter volumes recovering from trough
failure_condition: In the two weeks after TRANSIT first prints above -45, the 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its preceding 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL falling from +8.1 to +5.9 while PARKS rebounds from -41.6 to -20.0 jointly show households reallocating time out of the home into external venues; retail strips capture part of that reallocation, so the joint move predicts a higher forward RETAIL_REC mean.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls at least 1.5 points week-on-week while PARKS rises at least 15 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:between t-1w and t-0w RESIDENTIAL fell 2.2 points and PARKS rose 21.6 points
regime_hint: post-restriction reopening with voluntary out-of-home re-engagement
failure_condition: In weeks where RESIDENTIAL falls >=1.5 points and PARKS rises >=15 points together, the following 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not above its preceding 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Under the NSW restriction-easing regime in force at the decision date, WORKPLACES improving from -18.4 to -15.4 shows office return proceeding; office-adjacent food, cafe and discretionary retail spending follows with a two-to-four week lag, lifting the forward RETAIL_REC mean.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean improves for two consecutive weeks (t-1w -18.4 to t-0w -15.4)
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 3.0 points from t-1w (-18.4) to t-0w (-15.4)
regime_hint: restriction easing, density limits and mask mandates lifted before the decision date
failure_condition: WORKPLACES holds at or above -15.4 for four weeks but the forward 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC remains below its trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM normalising toward baseline (-3.9 at t-1w to -0.9 at t-0w) shows the household provisioning surge unwinding; trip and budget share previously diverted to grocery revert to discretionary retail, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from -3.9 at t-1w to -0.9 at t-0w while RETAIL_REC moved from -19.0 to -13.4
regime_hint: steady state provisioning with no restocking shock
failure_condition: In the week after GROCERY_PHARM moves toward zero, the forward 7-day mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than its trailing 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The t-2w and t-1w collapse in PARKS (-35.4, -41.6) is a weather and flood disruption layered on late-summer patterns; as that exogenous shock decays, outdoor trips resume and spill into adjacent retail strips, lifting RETAIL_REC in the first week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean rebounds at least 15 points off a local trough (-41.6 to -20.0)
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell to -41.6 at t-1w then rebounded 21.6 points to -20.0 at t-0w
regime_hint: seasonal transition out of late-summer weather and flood disruption
failure_condition: Following a PARKS rebound of at least 15 points off a local trough, RETAIL_REC does not rise in the next weekly mean.

mechanism_narrative: A rising infection wave in mid-March 2022 keeps a share of households voluntarily avoiding discretionary venues: RESIDENTIAL stays near +6 and TRANSIT stuck near -42, so RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks remains below its trailing 28-day mean despite formal restriction easing.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays at or above +5.5 while TRANSIT stays below -42 for at least three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:at t-0w RESIDENTIAL is +5.9 and TRANSIT is -42.3, both far from baseline
regime_hint: restriction easing with elevated voluntary avoidance during a rising infection wave
failure_condition: The forward 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC exceeds its trailing 28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL stays >=+5.5 and TRANSIT <=-42 for all four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES still 15.4 percent below baseline and RESIDENTIAL 5.9 percent above it show the commuter base has not returned; because office-anchored retail depends on that base, the forward RETAIL_REC mean stays below its trailing mean over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean remains at or below -15.0 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES is -15.4 and RESIDENTIAL +5.9 at t-0w, so work-from-home remains elevated
regime_hint: partial reopening with persistent work-from-home equilibrium
failure_condition: While WORKPLACES stays at or below -15.0, the forward 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC exceeds its preceding 14-day mean.
